=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline points

1. **Do not accept the "[STANDARD]" labels or the "Reviewer Efficiency Note."** These are the Seller's own unilateral tags. Nothing in the package shows that the Buyer agreed to any of them. Almost every material issue below sits under a "[STANDARD]" label. The note also asserts that we have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." We should reject that in writing so it cannot later be used as evidence of agreement. I have reviewed every position on its merits.
2. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its cover note.** Bluefen is described as "addressed," but the letter says no consent has been obtained. The DD-006 incident is called "not expected to be material," but the letter says the investigation is preliminary and its scope is unknown. The bonuses are called "a matter for the Seller," but they are Company liabilities and are missing from the funds flow.
3. **The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026, about six weeks old.** We need an updated letter and a bring-down before signing.

---

## A. Limitation package

### 1. General cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m), cl 12.1
- 20% for general warranties is within the market range. We can accept it or open at 30–35% as a trade.
- The real issue is scope. The cap must not apply to:
  - fundamental warranties (capacity, title, authority);
  - tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
  - the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark);
  - leakage or price-adjustment claims;
  - breach of covenants;
  - fraud or wilful concealment.

### 2. Thresholds, cl 12.2
- **Basket of AUD 250k (about 1.04% of price), deductible only:** this is high and purely Seller-friendly. Push for about AUD 120k (0.5%) as a tipping basket, so recovery runs from the first dollar once the threshold is crossed.
- **De minimis of AUD 25k:** reduce to AUD 10–15k. Related or same-cause claims should aggregate for de minimis purposes.
- Thresholds should not apply to fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.

### 3. Time limits, cl 12.3/13
- 18 months for general warranties is acceptable. It covers at least one full audit cycle.
- **Reject the default that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."** Reverse it so limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. Proposed periods:
  - Title and capacity: at least 7 years, or the statutory limitation period.
  - Tax: the ATO amendment period plus 6 months. This is unlimited for fraud or evasion.
  - Specific indemnities: matched to the risk. For example, DD-006 should run at least 3 years, given regulatory and class-action exposure.

### 4. Fundamental/title warranties under the same cap and time limits
- **Reject.** Title is the entire subject matter of the deal. If title fails, we have bought nothing, so recovery must be capped at 100% of the price (AUD 24m) with the long survival period above.
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept this.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature," cl 9.3/12.8/20.5
- **Carve out fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment** by the Seller, its officers or its advisers. Under NSW law the Seller cannot exclude liability for its own fraud. An attempt to do so invites a dispute, so express carve-outs are needed.
- Exclusive remedy should not cover specific performance, injunctions, leakage or price adjustment, or covenant breaches.
- Non-reliance clauses do not reliably exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under ACL s18. We should not be giving up that protection for pre-contract statements made outside the warranties. This includes the cover-note characterisations such as "Bluefen addressed" and "not material." If the Seller stands by those statements, they should become warranties.

---

## B. Disclosure framework

### 6. General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)
- **Reject.** This puts the cost of the Seller's information onto the Buyer and makes the warranties largely illusory. Our position:
  - Only specific disclosures that are fair and give sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter count.
  - Data room documents count only where specifically referenced in the Disclosure Letter.
  - No general disclosure of "publicly searchable corporate records." At most, accept limited specified searches as at a fixed date, such as ASIC and PPSR.
  - Disclosure does not qualify fundamental warranties, tax warranties or any indemnity.
  - The data room is to be frozen and supplied on USB/archive as an agreed index.
- **Clause 1.4 (non-admission):** acceptable in principle. However, we should ensure it does not weaken the effect of the specific disclosures as facts.

### 7. Buyer knowledge, cl 8.3
- **Reject in current form.** It reaches constructive knowledge ("discoverable") and advisers' knowledge, which would effectively wipe out the warranties.
- **Primary position:** express pro-sandbagging. Buyer knowledge does not limit claims.
- **Fallback:** actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals only, limited to facts fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and never applicable to indemnities.

---

## C. Specific issues

### 8. Bluefen consent (about AUD 3.6m revenue, about 30%), cl 3/6.3
- The letter confirms no final consent exists and that the cl 11.3 conditions have not been shown to be satisfied. "Addressed" is wrong.
- The Seller's mechanism treats the condition as satisfied on mere delivery of a written consent, even if the consent is conditional, partial, or comes with changed terms. Our position:
  - A **Condition Precedent** to Completion: unconditional written consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, acting reasonably.
  - Evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived.
  - No adverse amendments to the contract, such as pricing, term or termination rights.
  - The CP can be waived **only by the Buyer**.
  - The Seller uses **best (or all reasonable) endeavours**, not reasonable endeavours.
  - A long-stop date with a Buyer walk right.
  - A warranty at Completion that Bluefen has not given notice of termination or non-renewal.

### 9. Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m), cl 2/7
- **A release "following Completion" is unacceptable** on a debt-free/cash-free deal. A change of control under cl 8.1 may itself trigger default or acceleration.
- Required at Completion:
  - A payoff letter confirming the exact payout figure and per-diem amount.
  - Repayment directly from the purchase price via the funds flow, deducted as Debt.
  - A deed of release.
  - PPSR discharges and the release of any guarantees or share security, which we need to check: Riverlark may hold security over the shares, which also goes to title.
  - All delivered as Completion deliverables.

### 10. DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420k)
- These are Company obligations, not "a matter for the Seller."
- Treat them as **Transaction Expenses/Debt deducted from the price**, grossed up for:
  - employer superannuation (check whether the bonuses count as OTE);
  - payroll tax;
  - workers' compensation and other on-costs.
- They should be paid through the Company's payroll at or immediately after Completion, with PAYG withheld and funded by the Seller.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or later claims, including claims from employees who do not meet the continued-employment condition.
- The funds flow must itemise all of this.

### 11. Ironquay / SOW3 IP, cl 11.1
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 materials does **not pass** until every SOW3 fee has cleared. AUD 180k is shown as open. So the Company may not currently own IP it relies on.
- An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk: loss of the IP, infringement claims, or re-development costs. Our position:
  - Payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees before Completion, with a bank-verified receipt. This should be a CP or Completion deliverable, or at minimum the AUD 180k is retained or deducted.
  - A **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable.
  - A broadened indemnity for all Losses arising from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 materials. It should sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with at least 3–6 years survival.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident, cl 4.6/Sched 6
- About 1,240 personal records were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are unresolved.
- Under the Privacy Act NDB scheme, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days. The incident predates 22 September, so we need to know whether that assessment has been completed and whether the OAIC or affected individuals have been notified. A failure here is an exposure in its own right.
- "Not expected to be material" has no stated basis. Our position:
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment, follow forensic or legal advice, and notify if required, with Buyer consultation.
  - Delivery of the investigation report.
  - A **specific indemnity** covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party or class claims. It should sit outside the cap and basket, not be qualified by disclosure, and survive at least 3 years.
  - Consider an escrow or retention of about AUD 0.5–1m pending resolution.
  - The privacy and data warranties must not be read down by this disclosure.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k)
- Three linked renewals of identical value suggest a commitment split to stay below an approval threshold. The Seller's own letter says they should be read together.
- Points to raise:
  - Ask for dates, terms and termination rights, and for confirmation of whether the renewals were entered into or committed after the accounts date.
  - Any renewal after signing must require Buyer consent under the conduct-of-business covenants, with the relevant thresholds aggregated for related contracts.
  - Where the renewals are prepaid or accrued and not ordinary course, treat them as leakage or as a completion accounts adjustment.
  - Verify there is no related-party element.

### 14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Reject.** We need a standalone **tax indemnity/deed** for pre-Completion tax:
  - capped at 100% of the price;
  - no basket;
  - not qualified by disclosure;
  - survival aligned to the amendment period.
- IP warranties covering ownership and non-infringement are core value for an analytics business. Push for a higher sub-cap of 50–100% and longer survival. Ironquay shows these risks are real.

### 15. Title evidenced only by the share register (DD-012)
- The share register is the Seller's own record. The letter itself notes that the Buyer has not verified it. We require:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates;
  - the issue and transfer history;
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or other share rights exist;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares;
  - a release of any security over the shares, including from Riverlark;
  - signed share transfer forms at Completion.
- The title warranty is fundamental (see point 4).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller's characterisations ("notification only"; "no consent merely because shares are sold") need to be checked by our own team against the full change-of-control and "assignment" definitions. Some leases and contracts treat a change in control as a deemed assignment.
- Add any required notices as Completion deliverables or post-Completion covenants.
- Include a warranty that no consent is required beyond those listed.

### 17. Staleness and bring-down
- The letter is dated 22 September 2026.
- Require an updated Disclosure Letter at signing.
- Warranties should be repeated at Completion. Any new disclosures at Completion should **not** cure breaches; at most, they give the Buyer a termination right.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "[STANDARD]" labels / efficiency note | Pre-cleared; review only [OPEN] | Reject in writing; no positions agreed |
| 1 | General cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m), applies broadly | Accept 20–35% for **general warranties only** |
| 2 | Basket / de minimis | AUD 250k deductible / AUD 25k | About AUD 120k tipping / AUD 10–15k; aggregation |
| 3 | Time limits | 18m, default applies to all claims | 18m general only; title 7y+; tax = amendment period + 6m; indemnities 3y+ |
| 4 | Fundamental warranties | Same cap and time limits | 100% cap; long survival; not disclosable against |
| 5 | Limitations / non-reliance | All Claims of any nature | Carve out fraud/concealment, indemnities, tax, covenants, leakage |
| 6 | Disclosure | General disclosure of data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure only; none against fundamental/tax/indemnities |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Actual + constructive + advisers | Pro-sandbagging; fallback actual knowledge of named individuals |
| 8 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours | Buyer-waivable CP; unconditional consent; 11.3 satisfied; best endeavours |
| 9 | Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) | Release post-Completion | Payoff from price at Completion; deed of release; PPSR discharges |
| 10 | Bonuses (AUD 420k) | Seller's matter; not in funds flow | Deduct as Transaction Expenses incl. on-costs; payroll mechanics; indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Pay before Completion; confirmatory assignment; full IP-loss indemnity |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | NDB compliance covenant; report; uncapped specific indemnity; retention |
| 13 | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary course | Full details; aggregate consent thresholds; leakage/adjustment treatment |
| 14 | Tax / IP | General regime | Standalone tax indemnity; enhanced IP sub-cap and survival |
| 15 | Title | Share register only | Independent verification; release of share security; transfers at Completion |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify ourselves; notices as deliverables; consents warranty |
| 17 | Stale disclosure | Dated 22 Sept 2026 | Updated letter; bring-down; no cure by later disclosure |

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Disclosure and knowledge framework (6, 7).
2. Fundamental, tax and fraud carve-outs (4, 5, 14).
3. Price-protection items: Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay AUD 180k (9, 10, 11). Together these are about AUD 3.8m or more of value that must come off the price or be resolved at Completion.
4. Bluefen CP (8).
5. DD-006 indemnity and retention (12).
6. Threshold and cap tuning (1–3), which can be used as trading currency.

Our own diligence findings should be checked against the Seller's characterisations of the lease, Mossvale and Sandbar before we finalise these positions.

- Three linked renewals of identical value suggest a commitment split to stay below an approval threshold. The Seller's own letter says they should be read together.
- Points to raise:
  - Ask for dates, terms and termination rights, and for confirmation of whether the renewals were entered into or committed after the accounts date.
  - Any renewal after signing must require Buyer consent under the conduct-of-business covenants, with the relevant thresholds aggregated for related contracts.
  - Where the renewals are prepaid or accrued and not ordinary course, treat them as leakage or as a completion accounts adjustment.
  - Verify there is no related-party element.

### 14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Reject.** We need a standalone **tax indemnity/deed** for pre-Completion tax:
  - capped at 100% of the price;
  - no basket;
  - not qualified by disclosure;
  - survival aligned to the amendment period.
- IP warranties covering ownership and non-infringement are core value for an analytics business. Push for a higher sub-cap of 50–100% and longer survival. Ironquay shows these risks are real.

### 15. Title evidenced only by the share register (DD-012)
- The share register is the Seller's own record. The letter itself notes that the Buyer has not verified it. We require:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates;
  - the issue and transfer history;
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or other share rights exist;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares;
  - a release of any security over the shares, including from Riverlark;
  - signed share transfer forms at Completion.
- The title warranty is fundamental (see point 4).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller's characterisations ("notification only"; "no consent merely because shares are sold") need to be checked by our own team against the full change-of-control and "assignment" definitions. Some leases and contracts treat a change in control as a deemed assignment.
- Add any required notices as Completion deliverables or post-Completion covenants.
- Include a warranty that no consent is required beyond those listed.

### 17. Staleness and bring-down
- The letter is dated 22 September 2026.
- Require an updated Disclosure Letter at signing.
- Warranties should be repeated at Completion. Any new disclosures at Completion should **not** cure breaches; at most, they give the Buyer a termination right.
